note: The floors are the census sizes measured on the run that wrote them, and they are a ratchet
rather than a guess. A layer that reads fewer rows than its floor exits 3, not 0: a shrunken
denominator raises reported coverage while measuring less, which is the failure
planning/evidence/P4-acceptance.md records four separate times. Lowering one is a deliberate
edit with a reason in the commit, never a side effect of deleting rows.
lintFiles is the fourth floor and it was missing until 2026-08-21. The literals layer reads
the lint's scan count precisely because a lint that scanned nothing and a lint that found
nothing print the same exit code -- and then compared that count to nothing, so a lint
scanning 0 files reported clean and the whole gate exited 0. A required layer that measured
nothing read as a pass, which is worse than the exit-1 defect it sat beside.

layers.name: font-weight-face
layers.substitute: A SwiftUI Font is opaque — String(describing: Font.system(size: 13, weight: .semibold)) returns "Font(provider: SwiftUI.FontBox<SwiftUI.Font.SystemProvider>)", with no size, weight or face in it. Confirmed instead by: the TypeToken each text node names is recorded in tokens["type"] at apply time and checked against the measured line box by the type-metrics layer; DesignTokenParityTests pins the eight-role ladder against DESIGN.md; scripts/lint/no-raw-design-values.sh fails any font size that does not come off it. None of the three can see an ancestor .font() winning the cascade, and that residue is what this row is.
